gen_risks.description: Inadequate preparation and institutional instability within the implementing agency may hinder project success.
gen_risks.mitigation: Secure strong, sustained commitment from senior government leadership and establish incentives to sustain reforms beyond individual tenures.
gen_risks.evidence: Lack of adequate preparation and institutional stability

gen_risks.description: Failure to conduct thorough diagnostic and reform strategy may lead to project delays or failure.
gen_risks.mitigation: Conduct comprehensive diagnostic and reform strategy prior to project preparation.
gen_risks.evidence: FMIS projects often falter when foundational preconditions are not thoroughly assessed

gen_risks.description: Cybersecurity threats may compromise the integrity of government information systems.
gen_risks.mitigation: Develop and implement a robust information security and business continuity system.
gen_risks.evidence: Recent cyber incidents plaguing government entities

gen_risks.description: Inadequate data governance and analytics capabilities may limit the effectiveness of PFM reforms.
gen_risks.mitigation: Establish a data governance model and develop analytical capabilities through targeted training and structured model for building skills in PFM and data analytics.
gen_risks.evidence: PFM data production, use, and dissemination lacks an integrated and systematic approach

gen_risks.description: Climate-related risks may impact the project's progress and the government's ability to respond to climate-induced shocks.
gen_risks.mitigation: Enhance institutional resilience and service continuity through the development of an integrated information security and business continuity system.
gen_risks.evidence: Climate-related risks may impact the project's progress

gen_risks.description: Inefficient public investment management may lead to cost overruns and reduced project benefits.
gen_risks.mitigation: Strengthen public investment management through improved project preparation and approval processes.
gen_risks.evidence: Public investment averaged 2.7 percent of GDP in 2023, well below the level of its peers

gen_risks.description: Inadequate procurement practices may result in inefficient use of public resources.
gen_risks.mitigation: Modernize procurement practices and simplify processes to cut government purchase prices.

gen_risks.description: Limited fiscal space may constrain the government's ability to invest in priority areas.
gen_risks.mitigation: Improve revenue collection and reduce inefficient spending to increase fiscal space.
gen_risks.evidence: Guatemala faces challenges due to its low levels of public expenditure

gen_risks.description: Inadequate asset management may lead to inefficient use of state properties and reduced revenue.
gen_risks.mitigation: Improve asset management through better utilization and rationalization of state properties.
gen_risks.evidence: Guatemala spent Q452 million and generated Q608 million in real estate revenue in 2024

gen_risks.description: Inadequate human resources management may lead to inefficient use of public resources and reduced project benefits.
gen_risks.mitigation: Strengthen human resources management through strategic workforce planning and payroll audits.
gen_risks.evidence: Employee compensation is estimated to represent 40.9 percent of the country's total government expenditure

gt_risks.description: Technical design risks are considered Substantial. PFM reforms typically require a whole-of-government approach and involve complex, cross-cutting changes that are often difficult to implement; these challenges are further amplified when reforms involve development or integration of sophisticated information systems. Many of the anticipated efficiency gains depend heavily on interoperability of processes and seamless integration of information systems across institutions, and the involvement of multiple stakeholders adds further complexity and increases the potential for misalignment or implementation delays.
gt_risks.mitigation: The project design includes the development and application of well-defined, evidence-based PFM conceptual and governance models, informed by a diagnostic and reform strategy developed through stakeholder consultations, providing a clear and coherent framework expected to foster shared understanding, facilitate collaboration, and reduce fragmentation.

gt_risks.description: Institutional capacity for implementation and sustainability risks are Substantial. Given the complexity of PFM reforms, the project requires strong government commitment to ensure effective implementation and safeguard long-term sustainability. Since the project's beneficiaries extend beyond MINFIN, coordination challenges may arise during implementation.
gt_risks.mitigation: A PIU will be established within the Directorate of Public Treasury (DTP) for faster decision-making and improved coordination across MINFIN directorates. Component 3 will strengthen PIU operations (project management, financial management, procurement, monitoring, E&S risk management capacities); the Bank will provide training to the PIU and relevant stakeholders and facilitate change management mechanisms and a communications strategy. Coordination challenges involving multiple beneficiaries will be addressed through collaboration between MINFIN and SEGEPLAN via the Digital Transformation Commission.

gt_risks.description: Fiduciary risks are Substantial. This is due to DTP's limited experience with donor-funded projects and lack of recent engagement with World Bank operations; DTP has no prior experience implementing the Bank's procurement regulations, and the low value of anticipated contracts may limit interest from international firms, reducing competition. DTP has basic financial management systems in place but its unfamiliarity with the Bank's FM policies and requirements may pose risks to achieving the PDO, potentially leading to delays in activity execution.
gt_risks.mitigation: Measures include setting up a PIU with qualified personnel, offering procurement training to PIU and DTP staff, conducting market analysis to find potential providers, and preparing a simplified Project Procurement Strategy for Development (PPSD).
